reviews.comment: So much reading, homework, and quizzes. I found that there was a significant disconnect between these assignments and the exam and did not find them useful when studying. Lectures were boring and I stopped paying attention after the first 2 weeks, instead, I found the most success in doing previous year's exams. Great guy though nonetheless.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. I struggled to understand him sometimes since he speaks abstract. Some more demonstrations would have help to understand the concepts better. None the less, he is more than willing to help during office hours and even opened up other slots for students to come in and ask questions. Great guy

Awesome professor, workload isn't up to the professors in 206, he did iClicker for attendance points, easy if you pay attention. Engaging lectures with cool demonstrations sometimes. He really loves the subject and students, probably one of the best phys profs.

Honestly a great professor whose lectures were pretty informative and worth going to. If you're not lazy and go to all your classes and recitations, you can definitely handle this class. Only complaint is the class structure - making class and recitation attendance part of your grade is kinda annoying.

Professor Melconian is a very nice guy who truly cares about his students, but the class itself is not good and very poorly structured. The exams are the biggest weight, but the homework, iclicker, and recitation can all help your grade. Truthfully, all the professors use the same info on the slides.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally thought Dr. Melconian was awesome and hilarious. I learned a lot, but I also took full advantage of the resources offered (office hours, SI Sessions). It helped that the SI for Dr. Melconian was helpful and funny, because it meant that I was able to learn material in class and master it during SI. Overall, awesome professor, fun course

Dr. Melconian was just kinda mid. The course coordinators made all exams and took care of all grades except for iclicker so he didn't know a lot about what was going to be on the exam. He encourage questions often and made sure everyone was learning, but his teaching style just wasn't for me. Used pearson for homework and iclicker for attendence.

One of the most unfair professors I've had at A&M. He constantly goes back on his word, refuses to be accommodating even when he makes mistakes, and makes the class way more stressful than necessary. He was still trying to figure out how to teach the class but using grades as threats and being rude to students who request help is not okay.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He was fun and upbeat in class; I wish there was to say than that. Dr. Melconian has more to learn when it comes to consistency, being overcritical and indecent when grading (harsh attitude towards genuine mistakes), and his lab manuals. You will often have to drop the manual and require the aid of the TA. It's all needlessly stressful. My first C.

Lectures were mediocre, often sped through examples and left me very lost. He does University Physics which in my opinion is much better than Don't Panic. The grading system is broken (in a go0d way), you can literally get a 70 on every exam and still get a high A in the class. There's not many good profs for 206, so I'd say he's one of better ones

Professor Melconian truly cares about his students. Out of the Phys 218 classes he's definitely the best pick for University Physics. I went to A+ Tutoring which helped me a lot in class but Melconian's lectures actually go through exam questions which a lot of Physics professors don't do.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Melconian teaches the University Physics textbook and they grade using a Learning Objective system which doesn't use numbers and makes it easier to get credit, even if your final answer is wrong. There's two different types clicker quizzes: one that's anonymous and is graded on participation only and one that's graded on accuracy.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Melconian is your best choice for PHYS218 at TAMU hands down. Great physics prof! Very caring, makes lectures interesting with funny and sometimes goofy jokes, very chill and calm guy, and always understands his students questions. He answers questions to best ability, and if needed he will come back next lecture to retouch the question.

Dr. Melconian is a great professor. Sometimes his lectures get boring, but he really wants you to understand the concepts. The class is a lot to keep up with, but as long as you can do problems without looking up the answers you should be fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dan is the man. He will work with you as much as the the student willing to work.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Melconian was a great professor. He is Canadian so there is no difficult accent. He has taught at A&M for a long time and taught at a very appropriate level for the common exams. He is really good at explaining things. I took AP physics 1 in high-school so the course was quite easy for me, however if you haven't you should read the textbook.

Good but occasionally bland lectures. Certainly take Melconian or any University Physics teacher rather than Don't Panic teachers (textbook). University Physics is more homework, but you understand the material better and the tests are easier. Don't Panic is all conceptual and variable based, and the tests are much harder.

Melconian is a really good professor. Despite really smartass kids correcting him over minute details or just being annoying, he was really patient and heavily encouraged class participation. Overall, he does a really good job, is passionate about the subject, and wants his students to succeed. Plus the test grading system is pretty great.

PHYS 218 is a weed out class. Tests are common exams so it really does not matter what professor you have.  Dr. Melconian seems like a nice guy though! Can't say much about his teaching style. I hardly went to class. Instead I just went to A+. On track to make an A in the class as well.
I loved Dr. Melconian so much. He made physics easy to understand when I have never understood physics in my whole life. Very helpful, makes students feel comfortable asking questions in lecture.
Great Profesor really good at explaining stuff.  A very time demanding class.  Has formula sheets and was helpful at office hours.  I would sign up for any class he taught.

Prof frequently does nice  gestures like extend homework during the superbowl, hold extra office hours for those of us with tight schedules, and hold weekend reviews. His lectures are great, since they incorporate theory AND examples. Physics is never "blow-off", but he makes sure we learn and enjoy it. Answers e-mails within minutes. Great guy.

The reality is Physics 218 is a terrible course and will most likely be difficult no matter who you get. That being said Melconian is an awesome guy and professor and will do his best to explain the material, but you are going to have to learn to teach yourself as well due to the nature of the common exams.

This is one of the toughest classes I have taken. But Dr. Melconian is by far the best prof to take this class with. His lectures are helpful and full of examples. Would take him again for any physics class.

He is a genuinely nice guy who cares deeply for his students and whether or not they pass. He is available both in his office hours and about 20 minutes before and after class. His class tends to have the highest averages on the common exams out of all classes, which speaks for itself. He goes fast in lectures, but the examples come from the book.
I've heard terrible things about physics, and he made it almost easy.  Phenomenal at teaching, very helpful, and he understands that we can struggle with the concepts.

The best Physics professor you can get. The class will probably be the most difficult class you take hands down. He really does a good job of lightening the mood. He's hilarious and understands that the class is severely hard and that you have other classes you're working hard in. Very good at explaining things clearly and keeping the class engaged
